QF.id: Terminology in Equity and Debt Markets_24

question.text: A perpetual bond is characterized by:

answer.text: Having no fixed maturity date, paying interest indefinitely

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook describes a perpetual bond as a debt instrument that does not have a stated maturity date - the issuer has no obligation to redeem the principal, and investors are entitled to receive periodic coupon payments indefinitely. The Trap: "Maturing within 1 year" describes a short-term money-market instrument, not a perpetual bond. "Risk-free" is also wrong - perpetual bonds (for example, corporate AT1 bonds) carry credit and interest-rate risk; only the absence of a redemption date is what makes them "perpetual". Note: Source - NISM-Series-XV Research Analyst workbook (February 2026), p. 75.
